metadata.exam-title: Microsoft Azure AI Apps and Agents Developer Associate
metadata.description: Scenario-Based Study Guide for AI-103 certification - validates the ability to build intelligent applications and AI agents using Microsoft AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI Service, and related Azure AI services.

question.title: AI Foundry Hub Purpose
question.scenario: A development team is starting a new AI project and needs a centralized workspace to manage models, deployments, and connections across multiple Azure AI services.
question.question-text: Which Azure resource provides a centralized hub for managing AI models, deployments, and shared resources across a team?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the unified Azure AI management platform that replaced the previous Azure AI Studio branding.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Foundry hub is the centralized management plane for AI projects. It provides a unified workspace where teams can manage model deployments, shared connections (to Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, storage), compute resources, and security settings. Projects within the hub inherit these shared resources while maintaining isolation for their own assets.

ul.li: An AI Foundry hub can contain multiple projects, each with their own models, data, and evaluation runs.
Shared connections configured at the hub level (e.g., Azure OpenAI endpoints) are automatically available to all projects within the hub.
The hub manages RBAC at both hub and project levels, enabling fine-grained access control.

question.title: AI Foundry Project Structure
question.scenario: A company has multiple AI initiatives and wants to isolate resources for each initiative while sharing common infrastructure like model endpoints and data connections.
question.question-text: What is the recommended way to organize multiple AI initiatives within Azure AI Foundry while sharing common infrastructure?

choices.choice: Create multiple projects within a single AI Foundry hub
Create separate AI Foundry hubs for each initiative
Use a single project with multiple resource groups
Deploy each initiative in a separate Azure subscription

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider how the hub-and-project hierarchy enables resource sharing with initiative-level isolation.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Creating multiple projects within a single AI Foundry hub is the recommended approach. The hub provides shared infrastructure — model endpoints, data connections, compute — while each project maintains its own isolated scope for experiments, evaluations, and deployments. This avoids duplicating expensive resources across initiatives.

ul.li: Each project gets its own storage container for data assets and artifacts while sharing the hub's storage account.
Projects inherit hub-level connections but can also define project-specific connections not visible to other projects.
RBAC can be scoped to individual projects, so team members only access their own initiative's resources.

question.title: Model Catalog Deployment
question.scenario: A developer needs to deploy a foundation model from the AI Foundry model catalog. The model is a large language model that will serve production traffic with predictable latency requirements.
question.question-text: Which deployment type in Azure AI Foundry provides dedicated compute with guaranteed throughput for production workloads?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider which deployment model allocates reserved capacity measured in throughput units for consistent performance.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Provisioned Throughput Units (PTU) deployment allocates dedicated compute capacity for Azure OpenAI models, guaranteeing a fixed throughput rate. Unlike pay-as-you-go deployments that share capacity and may experience throttling, PTU deployments provide predictable latency and throughput, making them ideal for production workloads with consistent demand.

ul.li: PTU capacity is measured in units that correspond to a fixed number of tokens per minute for a specific model.
PTU deployments require a minimum commitment period and are billed hourly regardless of actual usage.
Serverless API (pay-as-you-go) is better for variable or bursty workloads where cost efficiency matters more than guaranteed throughput.

question.title: AI Foundry Evaluation Runs
question.scenario: A team has fine-tuned a model and wants to measure its performance on groundedness, relevance, and coherence before deploying it to production.
question.question-text: Which Azure AI Foundry feature allows you to run automated quality assessments of model outputs using built-in metrics like groundedness, relevance, and coherence?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the built-in assessment capability within AI Foundry that uses AI-assisted metrics to judge model output quality.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Foundry evaluation runs provide automated quality assessments using built-in AI-assisted metrics. These metrics include groundedness (is the response grounded in provided context), relevance (does it answer the question), coherence (is it well-structured), fluency, and similarity. Evaluations run against test datasets and produce scored results that help teams decide whether a model is production-ready.

ul.li: Evaluation runs can be triggered from the AI Foundry portal, the Azure AI SDK, or CI/CD pipelines for automated quality gates.
Custom evaluators can be defined using Python functions or prompty files to measure domain-specific quality criteria.
Risk and safety evaluations (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual content) are also available as built-in evaluators.

question.title: AI Foundry Connection Types
question.scenario: A developer is setting up an AI Foundry project and needs to connect to an Azure OpenAI resource, an Azure AI Search index, and an Azure Blob Storage account for grounding data.
question.question-text: At which level should shared connections be configured so that all projects in the workspace can access the same Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search resources?

choices.choice: At the Azure Active Directory tenant level
At the AI Foundry hub level

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider where in the hub-project hierarchy shared connections should live so that child projects automatically inherit them.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Shared connections should be configured at the AI Foundry hub level. Hub-level connections are automatically inherited by all projects within the hub, eliminating the need to configure them individually in each project. This centralizes credential management and ensures consistent access to common resources like Azure OpenAI endpoints and Azure AI Search indexes.

ul.li: Hub connections support multiple authentication types: API key, managed identity, and Azure AD (Entra ID) tokens.
Projects can override hub connections or add project-specific connections that are not shared with sibling projects.
Connections store credentials securely in the hub's associated Azure Key Vault.

question.title: AI Foundry Model Fine-Tuning
question.scenario: A healthcare company needs to fine-tune an Azure OpenAI GPT model on proprietary medical terminology and response patterns. They must ensure training data stays within their Azure tenant.
question.question-text: Which approach allows fine-tuning of Azure OpenAI models within AI Foundry while ensuring training data remains within the customer's Azure tenant?

choices.choice: Export the model weights and train locally
Use the Azure OpenAI fine-tuning API with training files uploaded to the customer's Azure OpenAI resource
Send training data to the OpenAI public API for fine-tuning
Use Azure Databricks to fine-tune the model independently

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the Azure-native fine-tuning path that keeps all data processing within the customer's own Azure resource boundaries.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Azure OpenAI fine-tuning API allows customers to upload training data (JSONL format) directly to their own Azure OpenAI resource. The fine-tuning job runs within Azure's infrastructure under the customer's tenant, meaning training data is not shared with OpenAI or other customers. The resulting fine-tuned model is deployed exclusively within the customer's Azure OpenAI resource.

ul.li: Fine-tuning supports GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini, and GPT-3.5-turbo models with supervised fine-tuning using JSONL training files.
Training data uploaded for fine-tuning is not used to train or improve Microsoft or OpenAI base models.
Fine-tuned models are billed at a higher per-token rate than base models and also incur hourly hosting costs once deployed.

question.title: AI Foundry Playground
question.scenario: A developer wants to quickly test different system messages and parameters for a deployed GPT-4o model without writing any code.
question.question-text: Which AI Foundry feature provides an interactive, no-code interface for testing prompts, adjusting parameters, and experimenting with deployed models?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the interactive web-based testing environment built directly into the AI Foundry portal.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The AI Foundry Playground is an interactive, browser-based interface within the AI Foundry portal. It allows developers to test prompts, configure system messages, adjust parameters (temperature, top_p, max tokens), add data sources for grounding, and experiment with chat completions — all without writing code. It supports chat, completions, and image generation modes.

ul.li: The Playground supports adding your own data via Azure AI Search, allowing you to test RAG scenarios interactively.
Conversations and configurations can be exported as code samples in Python, C#, JavaScript, and cURL.
The Playground also supports testing content filters and viewing which filter categories triggered on specific inputs or outputs.

question.title: AI Foundry Content Safety Integration
question.scenario: An enterprise is deploying a customer-facing chatbot and needs to ensure that both user inputs and model outputs are screened for harmful content categories including hate speech, violence, and self-harm.
question.question-text: How does Azure AI Foundry integrate content safety filtering with Azure OpenAI model deployments?

choices.choice: Content filters must be implemented manually in application code
A separate Azure Content Safety resource must be provisioned and called independently
Content filters are applied to the Azure AI Search index
Content filtering is built into Azure OpenAI deployments and can be configured with custom severity thresholds per category

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the integrated content filtering system that is part of the Azure OpenAI deployment itself, not a separate service call.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure OpenAI deployments include built-in content filtering that automatically screens both inputs (prompts) and outputs (completions). The content filter evaluates four categories — hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm — at configurable severity thresholds (low, medium, high). Custom content filter configurations can be created in AI Foundry and assigned to specific deployments, allowing different policies for different use cases.

ul.li: Content filters also include optional detectors for jailbreak attempts, protected material (text and code), and groundedness detection.
Custom blocklists can be added to filter specific terms or patterns beyond the built-in categories.
Content filter results are returned in the API response annotations, allowing applications to handle filtered content gracefully.

question.title: AI Foundry SDK Integration
question.scenario: A developer is building a Python application that needs to programmatically create an AI Foundry project, deploy a model, and run evaluations as part of an automated CI/CD pipeline.
question.question-text: Which SDK should the developer use to programmatically manage AI Foundry resources, deployments, and evaluations from Python code?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the dedicated Python SDK package designed specifically for managing AI Foundry projects and their resources programmatically.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Azure AI Foundry SDK (azure-ai-projects package) provides programmatic access to AI Foundry capabilities. It allows developers to create and manage projects, deploy models, run evaluations, manage connections, and integrate with tracing — all from Python code. This enables automation through CI/CD pipelines for continuous evaluation and deployment of AI models.

ul.li: The SDK integrates with azure-ai-inference for model calls and azure-ai-evaluation for running evaluation metrics.
It supports OpenTelemetry-based tracing that can be connected to Application Insights for observability.
The azure-ai-projects package works alongside the Azure Identity SDK for authentication via managed identity or service principals.

question.title: Azure OpenAI Chat Completions API
question.scenario: A developer is building a customer support chatbot and needs to send a conversation history to Azure OpenAI to generate contextual responses.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI API endpoint accepts a list of messages with roles (system, user, assistant) and returns a model-generated response?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about which API is specifically designed for multi-turn conversations with role-based message formatting.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Chat Completions API accepts a messages array where each message has a role (system, user, or assistant) and content. This structured format enables multi-turn conversations, system-level instructions, and context from previous turns. It is the primary API for GPT-4o, GPT-4, and GPT-3.5-turbo models on Azure OpenAI.

ul.li: The Chat Completions API also supports function/tool calling, JSON mode, and structured outputs for programmatic responses.
The older Completions API (single prompt in, completion out) is deprecated for newer models — Chat Completions is the standard.
Streaming responses use server-sent events (SSE) to deliver tokens incrementally as they are generated.

question.title: Semantic Kernel Architecture
question.scenario: A .NET developer wants to build an AI application that combines LLM calls with custom business logic plugins. The application needs to orchestrate multiple AI and non-AI steps in a single workflow.
question.question-text: Which framework provides a lightweight SDK for integrating LLMs with plugins and orchestrating AI workflows in .NET, Python, and Java?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider Microsoft's open-source orchestration SDK that uses a kernel-and-plugin architecture for AI application development.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Semantic Kernel is Microsoft's open-source SDK for building AI applications. It uses a kernel-and-plugin architecture where the kernel orchestrates AI service calls and plugin functions. Plugins contain native code functions and prompt templates that the kernel can invoke. Semantic Kernel supports .NET, Python, and Java, and integrates natively with Azure OpenAI and other LLM providers.

ul.li: Semantic Kernel plugins expose functions that the model can call via the function calling capability, enabling automatic orchestration.
The Kernel manages AI service configuration, plugin registration, and filter pipelines (pre/post function execution hooks).
Semantic Kernel integrates with AI Foundry for tracing and can be used alongside Azure AI Search for RAG patterns.

question.title: Structured Output with JSON Mode
question.scenario: An application needs to extract structured data from unstructured text using Azure OpenAI. The response must be valid JSON that conforms to a specific schema so it can be parsed programmatically.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI feature ensures the model output is valid JSON conforming to a developer-specified schema?

choices.choice: Structured Outputs with a JSON schema in response_format

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the response_format parameter that accepts a JSON schema definition to guarantee structurally valid output.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Structured Outputs allows developers to pass a JSON schema in the response_format parameter of the Chat Completions API. The model is then constrained to produce output that is valid JSON conforming to that schema. This guarantees parseable responses without relying on prompt engineering alone, eliminating JSON parsing errors in production applications.

ul.li: Structured Outputs uses constrained decoding at the token level, mathematically guaranteeing schema conformance — not just prompting the model to try.
The simpler JSON mode (response_format: {type: "json_object"}) guarantees valid JSON but does not enforce a specific schema.
Structured Outputs also works with function/tool definitions, ensuring tool call arguments match the declared parameter schema.

question.title: Azure OpenAI Streaming Responses
question.scenario: A web application displays AI-generated responses to users. The current implementation waits for the entire response before showing anything, resulting in a poor user experience with long wait times.
question.question-text: Which technique allows the application to display tokens incrementally as they are generated by the Azure OpenAI model?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the HTTP streaming mechanism that delivers partial responses as individual events while the model continues generating.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Enabling streaming in the Chat Completions API (stream: true) causes Azure OpenAI to return tokens incrementally via server-sent events (SSE). Each event contains a delta with one or more tokens. The application can render these tokens as they arrive, providing a responsive experience where users see text appearing in real-time instead of waiting for the complete response.

ul.li: Each streamed chunk is a ChatCompletionChunk object with a choices array containing delta content.
The final chunk includes a finish_reason (stop, length, content_filter, or tool_calls) indicating why generation ended.
Content filter results in streaming mode are returned in separate chunks and may lag behind the content chunks.

question.title: LangChain on Azure Integration
question.scenario: A Python developer is using LangChain to build a retrieval-augmented generation application. They need to use Azure OpenAI as the LLM provider and Azure AI Search as the vector store.
question.question-text: Which LangChain class should be used to integrate with Azure OpenAI's chat models while supporting Azure-specific authentication and endpoint configuration?

choices.choice: AzureChatOpenAI with azure_endpoint and api_version parameters

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the LangChain class specifically designed for Azure OpenAI's chat models, requiring Azure-specific parameters like endpoint and API version.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: AzureChatOpenAI is the LangChain class specifically designed for Azure OpenAI chat models. It requires Azure-specific parameters including azure_endpoint (the resource URL), api_version (Azure API version string), and azure_deployment (the deployment name). It supports both API key and Azure AD token authentication, making it the correct integration point for Azure OpenAI in LangChain applications.

ul.li: AzureChatOpenAI is in the langchain-openai package and extends the base ChatOpenAI with Azure-specific configuration.
For Azure AI Search as a vector store, LangChain provides the AzureSearch class in langchain-community.
Azure AD authentication can use DefaultAzureCredential for managed identity support in production deployments.

question.title: Token Management and Limits
question.scenario: An application using GPT-4o is experiencing errors when processing long documents. The error message indicates the combined input and output tokens exceed the model's context window.
question.question-text: What is the most effective approach to handle documents that exceed the model's context window in a chat completions call?

choices.choice: Switch to a model with a larger context window or implement chunking with summarization
Set max_tokens to a higher value

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider strategies that either expand the available context window or reduce the input to fit within the current model's limits.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: When documents exceed a model's context window, two primary strategies work: (1) switch to a model with a larger context window (e.g., GPT-4o supports 128K tokens), or (2) implement chunking — break the document into smaller pieces, summarize or process each chunk, and combine results. For retrieval scenarios, RAG with embeddings and vector search can surface only relevant chunks rather than the entire document.

ul.li: The context window includes both input tokens (system message + messages + tools) and output tokens (max_tokens).
Map-reduce and refine are common chunking patterns: map-reduce processes chunks independently then combines; refine iteratively updates a running summary.
Tiktoken is the standard tokenizer library for counting tokens before making API calls to avoid context window errors.

question.title: Azure OpenAI Authentication
question.scenario: A developer is deploying an application to Azure App Service and wants to authenticate to Azure OpenAI without managing API keys. The application should use the platform's identity capabilities.
question.question-text: Which authentication method allows an Azure-hosted application to access Azure OpenAI without storing or managing API keys?

choices.choice: Store the API key in Azure Key Vault
Use a shared access signature (SAS) token
Use managed identity with Azure AD (Entra ID) authentication
Embed the API key in environment variables

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the Azure identity feature that assigns an identity to a hosted service, allowing it to authenticate to other Azure resources without credentials in code.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Managed identity with Azure AD (Entra ID) authentication allows Azure-hosted applications to authenticate to Azure OpenAI without any credentials in code or configuration. The Azure platform automatically manages the identity and token lifecycle. The application uses DefaultAzureCredential or ManagedIdentityCredential to obtain tokens, and Azure OpenAI validates them via RBAC role assignments (e.g., Cognitive Services OpenAI User).

ul.li: System-assigned managed identity is tied to the specific App Service instance; user-assigned managed identity can be shared across services.
The Cognitive Services OpenAI User role grants access to make inference calls; Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor also allows deployment management.
DefaultAzureCredential tries managed identity, environment variables, Azure CLI, and other providers in order, making it work in both local dev and production.

question.title: Responsible AI Transparency
question.scenario: A company is building a public-facing AI application and needs to comply with Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard. They must ensure users understand when they are interacting with AI and what limitations exist.
question.question-text: Which Responsible AI practice requires informing users about the AI system's capabilities, limitations, and the role of AI in generating responses?

choices.choice: Transparency and disclosure through a transparency note

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Responsible AI principle that focuses on making AI behavior understandable and disclosing AI involvement to end users.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Transparency and disclosure is a core Responsible AI principle that requires applications to clearly inform users when AI is involved, what the system can and cannot do, and what its known limitations are. A transparency note documents intended uses, limitations, and potential biases. Microsoft's Responsible AI Standard mandates this for all customer-facing AI applications.

ul.li: Transparency notes for Azure AI services are published by Microsoft and cover each service's intended uses, limitations, and best practices.
Applications should disclose AI-generated content, allow users to provide feedback, and provide mechanisms to escalate to human support.
The six Microsoft Responsible AI principles are: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, and accountability.

question.title: Function Calling Basics
question.scenario: A developer wants their Azure OpenAI chatbot to look up real-time product inventory when a customer asks about availability. The inventory data is stored in an external database.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI feature allows the model to indicate that it needs to call an external function, such as a database lookup, to answer a user's question?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the API feature where you declare available tools and the model decides when to invoke them based on user intent.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Function calling (tool use) allows developers to describe available functions to the model using JSON schema definitions. When the model determines a function call is needed to answer a user's question, it returns a tool_calls response with the function name and arguments. The application then executes the function, sends the results back, and the model generates a final response incorporating the function output.

ul.li: The model never executes functions directly — it outputs a structured request that the application must handle and return results for.
tool_choice can be set to "auto" (model decides), "required" (must call a tool), "none" (no tools), or a specific function name.
Parallel function calling allows the model to request multiple function calls in a single response for efficiency.

question.title: Azure AI Agent Service
question.scenario: A company wants to build an AI agent that can autonomously research topics, write code, execute it, and summarize findings. They need a managed service that handles agent orchestration, tool execution, and conversation state.
question.question-text: Which Azure service provides a fully managed platform for building AI agents with built-in tool execution, file handling, and conversation thread management?

choices.choice: Azure Logic Apps with AI connectors
Azure Kubernetes Service with custom agent code

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the managed Azure service specifically designed for building and hosting AI agents with built-in orchestration capabilities.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Agent Service is a fully managed platform for building AI agents. It handles agent orchestration, tool execution (code interpreter, file search, custom functions), conversation thread management, and state persistence. Developers define the agent's instructions, tools, and model, and the service manages the execution loop — the agent autonomously decides which tools to use and when.

ul.li: Built-in tools include Code Interpreter (executes Python in a sandbox), File Search (searches uploaded documents), and custom function tools.
Threads maintain conversation history and are independent of the agent definition, enabling persistent multi-session interactions.
Runs execute the agent against a thread, with the service handling the tool execution loop until the agent produces a final response.

question.title: Semantic Kernel Plugin Architecture
question.scenario: A developer is using Semantic Kernel to build an agent that needs to access a CRM system, send emails, and query a knowledge base. Each capability should be modular and reusable.
question.question-text: In Semantic Kernel, what is the architectural unit that encapsulates a set of related functions that can be exposed to the AI model for automatic invocation?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the modular unit in Semantic Kernel that groups related functions and can be registered with the kernel for AI-driven invocation.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: A Semantic Kernel plugin is a collection of related functions that are registered with the kernel. Plugins can contain native code functions (annotated methods in C#/Python) and prompt-based functions (prompty templates). When automatic function calling is enabled, the kernel exposes plugin functions to the model, which can choose to invoke them based on user intent. This modular design enables reusable capabilities across different agents.

ul.li: Native functions use decorators (@kernel_function in Python, [KernelFunction] in C#) with descriptions that help the model understand when to call them.
The kernel's function calling behavior can be set to auto (model decides), required, or none, similar to Azure OpenAI's tool_choice.
Filters can intercept function calls before and after execution for logging, validation, or modification of arguments and results.

question.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration
question.scenario: A development team is building a complex workflow where multiple specialized AI agents need to collaborate — one for research, one for code generation, and one for review. The agents must pass context between each other.
question.question-text: Which framework pattern enables multiple specialized AI agents to collaborate, share context, and hand off tasks in a coordinated workflow?

choices.choice: Single agent with multiple system messages
Parallel independent API calls with result aggregation
Multi-agent orchestration with agent chat and handoff protocols
Sequential prompt chaining without agent state

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the architectural pattern where distinct agents with different specializations communicate through structured handoff and shared conversation context.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Multi-agent orchestration uses distinct agents with specialized roles that collaborate through agent chat and handoff protocols. Frameworks like Semantic Kernel's Agent Chat and AutoGen enable this pattern. Each agent has its own instructions, tools, and model configuration. A group chat or orchestrator manages turn-taking, context sharing, and task handoff between agents until the workflow objective is achieved.

ul.li: Semantic Kernel provides AgentGroupChat with selection and termination strategies for multi-agent conversations.
AutoGen supports flexible conversation patterns including round-robin, selector-based, and custom orchestration topologies.
Azure AI Agent Service supports multi-agent workflows through its thread and run architecture, where different agents can process the same thread.

question.title: Code Interpreter Tool
question.scenario: An AI agent needs to analyze a CSV file uploaded by a user, perform statistical calculations, and generate a chart. The agent should execute code in a sandboxed environment.
question.question-text: Which built-in tool in Azure AI Agent Service allows agents to write and execute Python code in a sandboxed environment to process files and generate visualizations?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the sandboxed execution environment that lets an agent run dynamically generated Python code on uploaded data.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Code Interpreter tool provides a sandboxed Python execution environment within Azure AI Agent Service. Agents can write and execute Python code to process uploaded files, perform calculations, generate charts, and create output files. The sandbox includes common data science libraries (pandas, matplotlib, numpy) and runs in isolation for security. File outputs are returned as downloadable attachments.

ul.li: Code Interpreter sessions are ephemeral — files and state are lost when the run completes, so important outputs must be downloaded.
The sandbox supports common file formats: CSV, JSON, Excel, PDF, images, and more for both input and output.
Each Code Interpreter invocation has execution time and memory limits to prevent runaway code.

question.title: Agent Conversation Threads
question.scenario: A customer service agent needs to maintain conversation context across multiple interactions. When a customer returns the next day, the agent should remember the previous conversation and any files that were shared.
question.question-text: In Azure AI Agent Service, which resource persists conversation history and file references across multiple interactions with an agent?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the persistent conversation resource in the Agent Service that stores messages and file attachments independently of any single run.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: A conversation thread in Azure AI Agent Service is a persistent resource that stores the full message history and file references. Threads are independent of the agent — the same thread can be processed by different agents, and the same agent can have many threads. When a new run is created on an existing thread, the agent has access to all previous messages and files, enabling multi-session continuity.

ul.li: Threads automatically manage context window limits by truncating older messages when the history exceeds the model's capacity.
Messages in a thread can include text, file attachments, and image content, all of which persist across runs.
Thread-level metadata (key-value pairs) can be used to store application-specific state like customer IDs or session tags.

question.title: Agent Grounding with Bing Search
question.scenario: An AI agent needs to answer questions about current events and recent developments that are not in the model's training data. The agent should be able to search the web for up-to-date information.
question.question-text: Which tool integration enables an Azure AI agent to ground its responses with real-time web search results for current information?

choices.choice: Azure AI Search with a static index
Azure OpenAI fine-tuning with recent data

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the web search tool that provides real-time internet search results for grounding agent responses with current information.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Bing Search grounding tool integrates with Azure AI Agent Service and Azure OpenAI to provide real-time web search capabilities. When enabled, the agent can search the web for current information, ground its responses in search results, and provide citations. This is essential for questions about current events, recent product releases, or any information beyond the model's training data cutoff.

ul.li: Bing grounding requires a Bing Search resource in Azure and must be configured as a connection in the AI Foundry project.
Search results include source URLs that can be returned as citations in the agent's response for verifiability.
Bing grounding is billed per search transaction and is separate from the Azure OpenAI model inference costs.

question.title: Parallel Function Calling
question.scenario: An AI assistant needs to look up weather, calendar events, and traffic conditions simultaneously to plan a user's commute. Each lookup is independent of the others.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI capability allows the model to request multiple independent function calls in a single response to improve efficiency?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the function calling feature that allows the model to output multiple tool_calls in a single response when the calls are independent.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Parallel function calling allows the model to include multiple tool_calls in a single response when it determines that several independent functions need to be called. The application can then execute all functions concurrently and return all results in a single follow-up message. This reduces round trips and latency compared to sequential function calling where each call requires a separate model invocation.

ul.li: Each tool call in a parallel response has a unique tool_call_id that must be matched when returning results.
Parallel function calling can be disabled by setting parallel_tool_calls to false if sequential execution is required.
The model determines parallelism based on function descriptions and the user's query — developers don't control which calls are parallelized.

question.title: Agent Error Handling
question.scenario: An AI agent occasionally encounters tool execution failures — API timeouts, permission errors, and invalid parameters. The agent needs to handle these gracefully without crashing or producing hallucinated results.
question.question-text: What is the recommended approach for handling tool execution failures in an AI agent built with Semantic Kernel?

choices.choice: Return the error details to the model as a tool result so it can adapt its approach
Let the model retry the same call automatically
Ignore the error and let the model generate a response without the tool result

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about giving the model visibility into what went wrong so it can decide whether to retry, try a different approach, or inform the user.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The recommended approach is to return error details as the tool result message to the model. This gives the model the information it needs to adapt — it might retry with corrected parameters, try an alternative tool, or inform the user about the limitation. Semantic Kernel's function invocation filters allow intercepting failures, logging them, and formatting error responses before they reach the model.

ul.li: Semantic Kernel's auto function calling behavior includes configurable retry limits to prevent infinite tool-call loops.
Function invocation filters (IFunctionInvocationFilter) provide pre/post execution hooks for error handling, logging, and result transformation.
Structured error responses (e.g., JSON with error_code and message) help the model make better decisions than raw stack traces.

question.title: RAG Pattern Overview
question.scenario: A company wants their AI chatbot to answer questions using proprietary company documentation that was not part of the model's training data.
question.question-text: Which design pattern augments LLM responses with relevant information retrieved from an external knowledge base at query time?

choices.choice: Fine-tuning the model on company data

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the pattern that retrieves relevant documents at query time and includes them in the prompt as context for the model to use.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) retrieves relevant documents from an external knowledge base at query time and includes them in the prompt context. The model then generates responses grounded in the retrieved information. RAG avoids the cost and staleness of fine-tuning, works with any document corpus, and ensures responses are based on current, authoritative sources rather than the model's training data alone.

ul.li: RAG involves three stages: indexing (chunking and embedding documents), retrieval (finding relevant chunks for a query), and generation (LLM response using retrieved context).
RAG is preferred over fine-tuning when the knowledge base changes frequently, since updating a search index is cheaper than retraining a model.
Hybrid retrieval (combining keyword search with vector similarity) typically outperforms either method alone.

question.title: Azure AI Search Vector Index
question.scenario: A developer is implementing a RAG solution and needs to store document embeddings for semantic search. They want to combine vector similarity with traditional keyword search for better retrieval quality.
question.question-text: Which Azure service provides both vector search and keyword search capabilities in a single index for hybrid retrieval in RAG applications?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Azure search service that natively supports vector fields alongside traditional text fields for hybrid search scenarios.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Search provides integrated vector and keyword search in a single index. Vector fields store embeddings for semantic similarity search, while text fields support traditional BM25 keyword search. Hybrid search combines both signals using Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) to produce results that leverage both semantic understanding and keyword matching. This makes it the primary Azure service for RAG retrieval.

ul.li: Azure AI Search supports multiple vector search algorithms: HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) for approximate nearest neighbor and exhaustive KNN for exact search.
Semantic ranker is an optional L2 re-ranking stage that uses a Microsoft-trained model to reorder results by semantic relevance.
Integrated vectorization can automatically generate embeddings at indexing and query time using a configured Azure OpenAI embedding model.

question.title: Document Chunking Strategies
question.scenario: A team is indexing a large corpus of technical documentation for RAG. They find that the default chunking strategy produces chunks that split sentences mid-thought, leading to poor retrieval quality.
question.question-text: Which chunking strategy preserves semantic coherence by respecting natural document boundaries like paragraphs and sections?

choices.choice: Semantic chunking based on document structure and meaning boundaries

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about chunking approaches that use document structure (headings, paragraphs) and semantic boundaries rather than arbitrary character counts.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Semantic chunking splits documents at natural boundaries — paragraph breaks, section headings, topic shifts — rather than at fixed character counts. This preserves the coherence of ideas within each chunk, leading to better retrieval quality because each chunk contains a complete thought. Azure AI Search's integrated data chunking skill and Document Intelligence layout analysis both support structure-aware chunking.

ul.li: Azure AI Document Intelligence's layout model extracts document structure (headings, paragraphs, tables) that can be used as chunking boundaries.
Overlap between chunks (e.g., 10-15% of the previous chunk repeated) helps preserve context at chunk boundaries for fixed-size strategies.
Chunk size should balance granularity (smaller chunks = more precise retrieval) with context (larger chunks = more context per result).

question.title: Embeddings for Semantic Search
question.scenario: A developer needs to convert text documents and user queries into numerical vectors so that semantically similar content can be found using vector distance calculations.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI API converts text into dense numerical vectors that capture semantic meaning for use in similarity search?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider which API specifically produces vector representations of text for use in similarity and search applications.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The Azure OpenAI Embeddings API converts text into dense numerical vectors (embeddings) that capture semantic meaning. Texts with similar meanings produce vectors that are close together in the embedding space. These vectors can be stored in a vector database or search index and queried using cosine similarity or other distance metrics to find semantically relevant content, which is the foundation of semantic search in RAG applications.

ul.li: Azure OpenAI offers text-embedding-ada-002 (1536 dimensions) and the newer text-embedding-3-small/large models with configurable dimensions.
The same embedding model must be used for both indexing documents and encoding queries to ensure vector comparability.
Embedding models have token limits per input — long documents must be chunked before embedding, not embedded as a whole.

question.title: Advanced RAG with Semantic Ranker
question.scenario: A RAG application retrieves relevant documents using hybrid search, but users report that the top results sometimes include tangentially related content that dilutes the model's response quality.
question.question-text: Which Azure AI Search feature applies a secondary re-ranking step using a deep learning model to improve the relevance ordering of search results?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the L2 re-ranking capability in Azure AI Search that uses a Microsoft-trained language model to re-order results by semantic relevance.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Semantic ranker is an Azure AI Search feature that applies a secondary re-ranking step after initial retrieval. It uses a Microsoft-trained deep learning model to re-score and re-order results based on semantic relevance to the query. This improves precision by pushing the most semantically relevant results to the top, which is especially valuable when the initial retrieval returns a mix of highly and marginally relevant documents.

ul.li: Semantic ranker works on the top 50 results from the initial retrieval stage (BM25, vector, or hybrid) and re-orders them.
It also produces semantic captions (extractive snippets highlighting the most relevant passage) and semantic answers (direct answer extraction).
Semantic ranker requires a semantic configuration on the index that specifies which fields to analyze for re-ranking.

question.title: On Your Data with Azure OpenAI
question.scenario: A developer wants to quickly add document grounding to an Azure OpenAI chatbot without building a custom retrieval pipeline. The documents are already indexed in Azure AI Search.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI feature allows you to add an Azure AI Search data source directly in the Chat Completions API call for built-in RAG?

choices.choice: System message with pasted document text

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Azure OpenAI feature that integrates a data source connection directly into the API call, handling retrieval and grounding automatically.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure OpenAI On Your Data allows developers to specify a data source (such as Azure AI Search, Azure Blob Storage, or Azure Cosmos DB) directly in the Chat Completions API call. The service automatically retrieves relevant documents, includes them as context, and generates grounded responses with citations. This eliminates the need to build a custom retrieval pipeline — Azure OpenAI handles the RAG orchestration internally.

ul.li: On Your Data supports multiple data sources including Azure AI Search (with vector, semantic, and keyword search), uploaded files, and Cosmos DB.
The data_sources parameter in the API request configures the connection, authentication, search type, and number of documents to retrieve.
Responses include citations with document references, and the strictness parameter controls how closely the model adheres to retrieved content vs. its training knowledge.

question.title: Azure AI Search Skillsets
question.scenario: A company needs to index a large collection of PDF documents for RAG. The documents contain text, tables, and images that need to be extracted, chunked, and enriched with embeddings before indexing.
question.question-text: Which Azure AI Search feature defines a pipeline of AI transformations that extract, enrich, and process content during the document indexing process?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the indexer pipeline component that chains together AI skills (OCR, text extraction, embedding generation) to process documents as they are indexed.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: An AI enrichment skillset in Azure AI Search defines a pipeline of AI transformations applied during indexing. Skills can include OCR (extracting text from images), text splitting (chunking), key phrase extraction, entity recognition, language detection, and embedding generation. The skillset is attached to an indexer, which processes source documents through the skill pipeline before writing enriched content to the search index.

ul.li: Built-in skills include Text Split (chunking), Azure OpenAI Embedding, OCR, Document Extraction, Entity Recognition, and more.
Custom skills can call external REST APIs or Azure Functions for domain-specific processing not covered by built-in skills.
The knowledge store feature allows skillset outputs to be projected to Azure Storage (tables or blobs) in addition to the search index.

question.title: RAG Groundedness Evaluation
question.scenario: A RAG application is in production but users report occasional responses that include information not present in the retrieved documents. The team needs to measure and reduce these groundedness failures.
question.question-text: Which evaluation metric specifically measures whether an AI-generated response is supported by the retrieved context documents, detecting fabricated information?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the evaluation metric that checks whether every claim in the response can be traced back to the provided context documents.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The groundedness score measures whether the model's response is factually supported by the retrieved context documents. A low groundedness score indicates the model fabricated information (hallucinated) that is not present in the source material. Azure AI Foundry's evaluation framework includes a built-in groundedness evaluator that uses an AI judge to score each response against its source context on a 1-5 scale.

ul.li: Groundedness detection can also be enabled at the Azure OpenAI content filter level for real-time detection during inference.
The evaluation requires three inputs: the query, the retrieved context, and the generated response — all three are needed to assess groundedness.
Improving groundedness often involves better chunking strategies, increasing the number of retrieved documents, and adding system message instructions to cite sources.

question.title: GPT-4o Vision Capabilities
question.scenario: A retail company wants to build an application that analyzes product images uploaded by customers and generates detailed text descriptions for accessibility and cataloging.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI model supports both text and image inputs in the same Chat Completions request for vision-language tasks?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the multimodal model that natively processes both text and image inputs in a single conversation turn.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: GPT-4o is a multimodal model that processes both text and image inputs within the Chat Completions API. Images can be included as base64-encoded content or as URLs in the messages array. The model can analyze, describe, and reason about images alongside text, enabling use cases like image captioning, visual question answering, document analysis, and accessibility descriptions.

ul.li: Image inputs consume tokens based on the image resolution — the detail parameter (low/high/auto) controls the resolution and token cost.
Multiple images can be included in a single message for comparison or multi-image reasoning tasks.
GPT-4o vision works with the same API endpoint as text-only requests — no separate vision endpoint is needed.

question.title: DALL-E Image Generation
question.scenario: A marketing team wants to generate custom product images from text descriptions for social media campaigns using Azure OpenAI.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI model generates images from text prompts and supports specifying image size, quality, and style parameters?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Azure OpenAI model specifically designed for generating images from natural language descriptions.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: DALL-E 3 is Azure OpenAI's image generation model that creates images from text prompts. It supports parameters for image size (1024x1024, 1024x1792, 1792x1024), quality (standard or hd), and style (vivid or natural). DALL-E 3 includes built-in prompt rewriting that enhances the input prompt for better results, and all generated images include C2PA content credentials for provenance tracking.

ul.li: DALL-E 3's prompt rewriting can be influenced by including specific style instructions in the prompt; the revised_prompt field in the response shows what was actually sent to the model.
Content filtering applies to both the text prompt (input) and the generated image (output), blocking harmful content in either direction.
Generated images are returned as URLs (valid for a limited time) or as base64-encoded data depending on the response_format parameter.

question.title: Vision with Document Analysis
question.scenario: An insurance company needs to extract structured data from claim forms that contain handwritten notes, tables, and stamps. The forms are scanned as images.
question.question-text: Which Azure AI service specializes in extracting structured data from documents including handwritten text, tables, and key-value pairs from scanned images?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the Azure AI service with prebuilt and custom models specifically designed for structured document data extraction.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) specializes in extracting structured data from documents. It provides prebuilt models for common document types (invoices, receipts, IDs) and a layout model that extracts text, tables, key-value pairs, and selection marks. It handles handwritten text, stamps, and complex layouts. Custom models can be trained for domain-specific document types not covered by prebuilt models.

ul.li: The layout model extracts document structure including headings, paragraphs, tables, and reading order — useful as a pre-processing step for RAG chunking.
Document Intelligence outputs include bounding box coordinates for each extracted element, enabling UI highlighting and verification workflows.
Custom classification models can automatically identify document types in a mixed batch before routing to the appropriate extraction model.

question.title: Whisper Speech-to-Text
question.scenario: A call center wants to transcribe customer service calls into text for analysis, quality assurance, and compliance auditing.
question.question-text: Which Azure OpenAI model converts spoken audio into text transcriptions with support for multiple languages?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the OpenAI model specifically trained for automatic speech recognition and transcription.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Whisper is a speech-to-text model available through Azure OpenAI that transcribes audio into text. It supports multiple languages and can handle accented speech, background noise, and domain-specific terminology. The API accepts audio files and returns transcriptions with optional timestamps. It supports both transcription (same language) and translation (to English) modes.

ul.li: Whisper supports audio formats including mp3, mp4, mpeg, mpga, m4a, wav, and webm with a 25 MB file size limit per request.
The prompt parameter can provide context (spelling of names, domain terms) to improve transcription accuracy for specialized content.
For real-time transcription, Azure AI Speech service provides streaming speech-to-text; Whisper is batch-oriented (file-in, text-out).

question.title: Multimodal RAG with Images
question.scenario: A technical documentation system needs to answer questions that reference both text content and diagrams in the documentation. The system should understand and reason about the visual content in diagrams alongside the surrounding text.
question.question-text: What is the recommended approach for implementing RAG that can retrieve and reason about both text chunks and image content from technical documentation?

choices.choice: Store only text and ignore images in the documentation
Index image descriptions and use a multimodal model (GPT-4o) to reason about retrieved text and image content together
Convert all images to text using OCR only
Store images in a separate system with no connection to the text search

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about combining image indexing with multimodal model capabilities to reason about both text and visual content in a unified retrieval and generation flow.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Multimodal RAG indexes both text chunks and image references (with generated descriptions or captions) in the search index. At retrieval time, relevant text and associated images are retrieved together. The generation step uses a multimodal model like GPT-4o that can process both the text context and the actual images, reasoning about diagrams, charts, and screenshots alongside the written content to provide comprehensive answers.

ul.li: Azure AI Document Intelligence can extract images from documents along with their positions, which can then be stored in blob storage and referenced in the search index.
Image embeddings (from models like Florence or CLIP) enable vector search over images, finding visually similar diagrams or matching text queries to relevant images.
GPT-4o's vision capability adds tokens for each image based on resolution, so the number and size of images in the prompt affect both latency and cost.

question.title: Image Input Token Costs
question.scenario: A developer is building an application that sends high-resolution product images to GPT-4o for analysis. The application is exceeding its token budget due to image processing costs.
question.question-text: Which parameter in the GPT-4o vision API controls the resolution level of image inputs to manage token consumption?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the image content parameter that offers preset resolution levels affecting how many tokens an image consumes.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The detail parameter on image content parts controls the resolution at which GPT-4o processes images. "low" uses a fixed 85-token representation regardless of image size, suitable for simple classification or description tasks. "high" processes the image at full resolution using multiple 512x512 tiles, consuming more tokens but enabling fine-grained analysis. "auto" lets the model choose based on the image size.

ul.li: In high detail mode, the image is first scaled to fit within 2048x2048, then divided into 512x512 tiles, each costing 170 tokens plus a base 85 tokens.
A 1024x1024 image in high detail mode consumes approximately 765 tokens (4 tiles x 170 + 85 base).
For cost optimization, resize images to the minimum resolution needed for the task before sending to the API.

question.title: Azure AI Speech Text-to-Speech
question.scenario: A language learning application needs to generate natural-sounding speech from text in multiple languages and voices so students can hear correct pronunciation.
question.question-text: Which Azure AI service converts text into natural-sounding speech with support for multiple languages, voices, and speaking styles?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Azure AI service specifically designed for synthesizing spoken audio from text input with customizable voice options.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Speech text-to-speech (TTS) converts text into natural-sounding speech. It supports over 400 neural voices across 140+ languages and dialects. Developers can control speaking style (cheerful, sad, angry), rate, pitch, and emphasis using SSML (Speech Synthesis Markup Language). Custom Neural Voice allows training a unique voice model on provided audio samples for brand-specific voice experiences.

ul.li: Neural TTS voices are generated by deep neural networks and sound significantly more natural than the older standard voices.
SSML provides fine-grained control: prosody (rate, pitch, volume), emphasis, breaks, phoneme pronunciation, and speaking style switching mid-sentence.
Real-time streaming TTS is available for interactive applications; batch synthesis is available for generating audio files at scale.

question.title: Multimodal Content Safety
question.scenario: An application accepts both text and image uploads from users for AI processing. The company needs to screen both modalities for harmful content before passing them to the AI model.
question.question-text: Which Azure service provides content safety screening for both text and image inputs, detecting categories like hate, violence, sexual content, and self-harm across modalities?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the dedicated Azure AI service for analyzing text and images against content safety categories with severity scoring.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Azure AI Content Safety provides multimodal content screening for both text and image inputs. It evaluates content across four harm categories — hate, sexual, violence, and self-harm — with severity levels (safe, low, medium, high). The service offers separate APIs for text analysis and image analysis, plus a prompt shields API that detects jailbreak attempts and indirect prompt injection attacks in AI application inputs.

ul.li: Content Safety can be called as a standalone API for pre-screening user inputs before they reach the AI model, adding a defense layer beyond the built-in Azure OpenAI filters.
Custom categories allow organizations to define domain-specific content policies beyond the four built-in harm categories.
The groundedness detection API identifies hallucinated content in AI-generated responses by comparing them against source documents.

question.title: System Message Purpose
question.scenario: A developer is building a customer support chatbot and wants to set the AI's persona, tone, and behavioral boundaries for all conversations.
question.question-text: Which component of the Chat Completions API message structure establishes the AI model's persona, behavioral guidelines, and response constraints?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the message role designed for developer-provided instructions that shape the model's behavior across the entire conversation.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The system message (role: "system") is the first message in the messages array and establishes the model's persona, behavioral guidelines, and constraints. It sets the tone, defines what the model should and should not do, specifies the response format, and provides context that persists across all turns. The model treats system message instructions as its operating parameters for the entire conversation.

ul.li: System messages should include: persona definition, task boundaries, safety instructions, output format requirements, and any domain-specific rules.
The system message is not immune to prompt injection — defense-in-depth with content filters and input validation is still needed.
Azure OpenAI's system message best practices recommend separating instructions into sections: role, capabilities, limitations, safety, and output format.

question.title: Few-Shot Prompting
question.scenario: A developer needs the model to classify customer feedback into specific categories (complaint, suggestion, praise, question). The model occasionally misclassifies edge cases when given only instructions.
question.question-text: Which prompting technique provides example input-output pairs within the prompt to guide the model's behavior on similar tasks?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the prompting technique that includes concrete examples of desired inputs and outputs to demonstrate the expected behavior pattern.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Few-shot prompting includes example input-output pairs within the prompt to demonstrate the desired behavior. For classification tasks, this means showing examples of each category with representative inputs. The model uses these examples to understand the pattern, format, and decision criteria without needing explicit rules for every edge case. Typically 3-5 well-chosen examples are sufficient for most tasks.

ul.li: Examples are typically provided as user/assistant message pairs in the conversation history, showing the expected interaction pattern.
Example selection matters: include edge cases, borderline examples, and examples from each category for balanced representation.
Few-shot prompting consumes tokens from the context window — balance the number of examples against available context for the actual input.

question.title: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
question.scenario: An AI application needs to solve multi-step math problems and logical reasoning tasks. Direct prompting produces incorrect final answers because the model skips intermediate reasoning steps.
question.question-text: Which prompting technique instructs the model to show its reasoning process step-by-step before providing a final answer?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the technique that explicitly asks the model to work through its reasoning process before arriving at a conclusion.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting instructs the model to explain its reasoning step-by-step before giving a final answer. This can be triggered by phrases like "Let's think step by step" or by providing examples that include reasoning steps. CoT significantly improves accuracy on math, logic, and multi-step reasoning tasks because it forces the model to decompose complex problems into manageable steps rather than jumping to conclusions.

ul.li: Zero-shot CoT ("Think step by step") works without examples; few-shot CoT includes examples with demonstrated reasoning chains.
CoT is most effective for tasks requiring multiple reasoning steps; it adds minimal value for simple factual recall or classification.
Tree-of-thought extends CoT by exploring multiple reasoning paths and selecting the best one, useful for planning and creative problem solving.

question.title: Temperature Parameter
question.scenario: A developer is building a code generation tool that needs to produce consistent, deterministic outputs. The same prompt should produce the same code every time.
question.question-text: Which parameter should be set to 0 or near 0 to make the model's output more deterministic and consistent?

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the sampling parameter that controls the randomness of the model's token selection, where lower values mean more deterministic output.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: The temperature parameter controls the randomness of the model's output. A temperature of 0 makes the model nearly deterministic by always selecting the highest-probability token. Higher temperatures (0.7-1.0) increase randomness and creativity. For code generation, factual Q&A, and extraction tasks where consistency is important, a low temperature (0-0.3) is recommended.

ul.li: Temperature and top_p both control randomness — Azure OpenAI recommends adjusting one but not both simultaneously.
Temperature 0 is not perfectly deterministic due to floating-point arithmetic in GPU computations, but it's as close as possible.
For creative writing, brainstorming, and diverse outputs, higher temperatures (0.7-1.0) are appropriate; for deterministic tasks, use 0-0.3.

question.title: Prompt Injection Defense
question.scenario: A public-facing chatbot is vulnerable to prompt injection attacks where malicious users embed instructions in their input to override the system message and make the model behave in unintended ways.
question.question-text: Which defense-in-depth strategy combines multiple layers to protect against prompt injection attacks in Azure OpenAI applications?

choices.choice: Rely solely on a strong system message with injection warnings
Use content filters, input validation, system message guardrails, and the Prompt Shields API together
Set temperature to 0 to prevent creative responses

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about combining multiple defensive layers — no single technique is sufficient against prompt injection on its own.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Defense-in-depth against prompt injection combines multiple layers: (1) system message guardrails that instruct the model to resist overrides, (2) Azure AI Content Safety's Prompt Shields API that detects jailbreak and injection attempts, (3) input validation and sanitization in application code, (4) Azure OpenAI content filters that screen inputs and outputs, and (5) output validation to ensure responses comply with expected formats. No single layer is sufficient — attackers can often bypass individual defenses.

ul.li: Prompt Shields detects two attack types: direct jailbreak attempts (user prompt attacks) and indirect prompt injection (malicious instructions embedded in retrieved documents).
Input delimiters (XML tags, triple backticks) in the system message help the model distinguish between instructions and user content, but are not foolproof.
Least-privilege responses — limiting what the model can do even if compromised (no tool calls without validation, no PII disclosure) — reduce the blast radius of successful injection.

question.title: Prompt Templates with Prompty
question.scenario: A team needs to manage and version their prompt templates alongside application code. They want a standardized format that includes model configuration, input variables, and the prompt text in a single file.
question.question-text: Which file format provides a standardized, version-controllable way to define prompt templates with embedded model configuration and input variables?

choices.choice: Prompty (.prompty) files with YAML frontmatter and Jinja2 templates

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the Microsoft-developed file format specifically designed for portable, self-contained prompt definitions that include model settings in their metadata.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Prompty (.prompty) files are a standardized format for defining prompt templates. Each file contains YAML frontmatter with model configuration (model name, parameters like temperature and max_tokens), input variable definitions, and the prompt template using Jinja2 syntax. Prompty files are plain text, version-controllable, and supported by Semantic Kernel, AI Foundry, and VS Code extensions for testing and execution.

ul.li: Prompty files can be loaded and executed directly by Semantic Kernel as prompt functions, or by the Prompty SDK in Python.
The YAML frontmatter supports specifying the model, API configuration, sample inputs for testing, and output format expectations.
Prompty integrates with AI Foundry evaluation — prompt templates can be evaluated against test datasets to measure quality metrics before deployment.

question.title: Output Format Instructions
question.scenario: A developer needs the model to always respond with a specific JSON structure containing fields for "sentiment", "confidence", and "summary" when analyzing customer reviews.
question.question-text: What is the most reliable way to ensure Azure OpenAI consistently returns responses in a specific JSON format with required fields?

choices.choice: Ask the model politely to use JSON
Use response_format with a JSON schema definition (Structured Outputs)

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Think about the API parameter that constrains the model's output at the decoding level to guarantee schema-conformant JSON.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Using response_format with a JSON schema definition (Structured Outputs) is the most reliable approach. It constrains the model's token generation to produce only valid JSON matching the specified schema. Unlike prompt-based instructions (which the model may occasionally ignore), Structured Outputs provides a mathematical guarantee of schema conformance, eliminating JSON parsing errors and missing field issues in production.

ul.li: Structured Outputs supports nested objects, arrays, enums, and required/optional fields — most JSON Schema features are available.
The first request with a new schema incurs a brief processing delay for schema compilation; subsequent requests with the same schema are faster.
Structured Outputs can be combined with system message instructions that describe the meaning of each field to improve content quality within the guaranteed structure.

question.title: Meta-Prompting for Complex Tasks
question.scenario: A developer is building an AI system that needs to handle a wide variety of complex tasks. Rather than writing individual prompts for each task, they want the model to decompose complex requests and generate its own specialized sub-prompts.
question.question-text: Which advanced prompting technique has the model decompose complex tasks and generate specialized sub-prompts for each component, orchestrating its own reasoning process?

choices.choice: Meta-prompting where the model plans and generates task-specific sub-prompts

hint.label: Brief Hint
hint.content: Consider the technique where the model acts as its own prompt engineer, breaking down complex requests and crafting targeted prompts for each sub-task.

hint.label: Complete Explanation
hint.content: Meta-prompting is an advanced technique where the model is instructed to decompose a complex task into sub-tasks and generate specialized prompts for each component. The model acts as its own orchestrator — it plans the approach, creates targeted sub-prompts, executes them (potentially with tool calls), and synthesizes the results. This technique is effective for open-ended, multi-faceted tasks where a single prompt cannot capture all requirements.

ul.li: Meta-prompting can be combined with function calling to create agentic loops where the model plans, executes tools, evaluates results, and iterates.
The technique works best with strong models (GPT-4o and above) that have sufficient reasoning capability to effectively decompose and plan.
Guard rails in the meta-prompt should limit recursion depth and provide fallback behavior to prevent runaway token consumption.
